text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 3 in history.
1703 - Robert Hooke, English scientist, died. A contributor to astronomy, chemistry and biology, he also discovered the law of elasticity, known as Hooke's law.
1792 - Robert Adam, Scottish architect and interior designer, died. One of the greatest neoclassical architects, he was much influenced by a visit to Rome.
1804 - Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, Italian painter and engraver, died.
1831 - George Pullman, American inventor of Pullman railway carriages, born.
1845 - Florida became the 27th state of the Union.
1847 - Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone, born in Scotland.
1861 - The serfdom, a form of slavery, was abolished in Russia.
1869 - Sir Henry Wood, founder of the annual Promenade concerts, born in London.
1875 - First performance of Bizet's opera "Carmen" took place at the Opera Comique, Paris.
1878 - The peace treaty at San Stefano was signed, ending the Russo-Turkish War and gaining independence for Serbia.
1886 - Treaty of Bucharest was signed bringing peace between Bulgaria and Serbia.
1911 - Jean Harlow, American film actress, born. She was nicknamed the "platinum blonde" after appearing in a film of the same name.
1918 - Germany and its allies signed the treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Russia, ending hostilities between them in World War One.
1924 - Mustafa Kemal continued his reforms to modernise Turkey, abolishing the Caliphate and expelling the Caliph and his family from the country.
1931 - The Star-Spangled Banner was adopted as the American national anthem.
1943 - 178 die in an accident at an air raid shelter in Bethnal Green, London.
1959 - Lou Costello (Louis Francis Cristillo), U.S. actor and comedian, partner of Bud Abbott, died.
1963 - A new constitution was approved in Senegal under which the president took over the powers of the prime minister.
1965 - Seretse Khama became the first premier of Bechuanaland.
1967 - Grenada became an associate state of Britain rather than a colony.
1969 - The three-man Apollo 9 spacecraft was launched from Cape Kennedy. The main aim of its 10-day flight was to test the lunar module in Earth's orbit.
1974 - A Turkish Airlines DC-10 crashed in a forest near Paris; all 346 aboard were killed.
1976 - Mozambique closed its border with Rhodesia and put its country on a war footing, after cross-border raids by Rhodesia on rebel bases.
1983 - Arthur Koestler, Hungarian-born writer who settled in Britain, died. A believer in euthanasia, he committed suicide with his wife.
1988 - In Britain, the Social Democrats and Liberals launched their new joint political party - the Social and Liberal Democrats (SLD).
1990 - A Panama bomb blast injured 16 U.S. servicemen and 10 Panamanians.
1991 - A United Airlines Boeing 737 crashed in Colorado; all 25 on board died.
1991 - Latvia and Estonia voted for independence in referendums.
1991 - Sao Tome and Principe elected former dissident Miguel Trovoada as president.
1995 - U.S. marines, firing cannons and machineguns as they left Somalia, killed several civilians and wounded dozens.
1996 - A Moslem suicide bomber blew apart 18 people on a Jerusalem bus and wounded 10 in a mirror-image of an attack one week ago.
